queries: Phaser 3.90 immutable source and license evidence
TypeScript ECS libraries suitable for deterministic spatial shop simulation
Cocos Creator 3.8 runtime license and mini-game platform support
Existing repository spatial logistics prototype and web-lite adapter reuse

candidates.name: Phaser 3.90.0
candidates.technicalFit: Approved only as the already-pinned web-lite development and QA renderer. The deterministic simulation remains DOM-free and engine-free so Phaser output is not treated as proof of publishability for any target mini-game platform.
securityRisks: Browser APIs must remain outside the shared simulation core
A web build must not be mislabeled as a mini-game package
attributionRequirements: Retain the Phaser copyright notice and MIT permission notice in distributed substantial copies

candidates.name: Miniplex 0.7.2
candidates.technicalFit: Framework-neutral TypeScript entity queries are compatible with the intended rule layer, but the first template needs a small stable-ID state graph rather than an ECS. Adding object-identity entity management would complicate deterministic saves and cross-runtime migration without reducing current code.
securityRisks: Additional dependency and API lifecycle for a feature set not required by the first template
attributionRequirements: If adopted later, retain the Miniplex copyright and MIT permission notice

candidates.name: bitECS 0.4.0
candidates.technicalFit: Its data-oriented queries and serialization are stronger than this low-entity-count shop needs. Version 0.4 is a documented API rewrite, and MPL file-level source obligations add release work that is avoidable for a compact original simulation.
securityRisks: Recent major API rewrite increases migration risk
Typed-array oriented storage would add conversion code for human-readable versioned saves
attributionRequirements: MPL-2.0 notices and source availability obligations would apply to covered files and modifications

candidates.name: Cocos Engine 3.8.8
candidates.license: MIT engine runtime; separate editor terms require review
candidates.technicalFit: The upstream runtime documents WeChat Mini Game and TikTok Mini Games support and remains the planned production renderer. It is not added to the web-lite template, and this evidence does not establish TapTap packaging or resolve separate Cocos Creator editor terms.
securityRisks: Editor terms must be reviewed separately from the MIT runtime license before production redistribution
TapTap packaging still requires an independently verified adapter and real-device QA
attributionRequirements: Retain the Cocos Engine copyright and MIT permission notice for substantial runtime copies
Review and comply with applicable Cocos Creator editor terms before production use

rationale: Reuse only the repository's existing pinned Phaser renderer for browser development and QA. Keep the spatial-shop simulation as small original pure TypeScript because the evaluated ECS libraries add dependency, save-format, migration, or licensing cost without solving a current bottleneck. Preserve a renderer boundary for a later separately verified Cocos production adapter; do not claim any mini-game platform is publishable from this web-lite work.
